subject: Numeracy
title: Our class graph
objectives: Children will sort themselves or objects into groups by a simple choice.
Children will say which group has more.
content: Sorting children or objects by a simple choice, forming lines and saying which line has more.
teachingActivities: Make real graphs with children and objects; line up neatly at one end; ask "Which line has more?" and count to check.
learnerActivities: Choose between two things, stand or place objects in lines, compare lines and count a line.
resources: Picture cards of two favourite fruits
A string line on the floor
assessment: Check whether each child joins a group according to a choice and says which group has more.
expectedOutcomes: Joins a group according to a choice.
Points to the group with more.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: choosing and respecting differences

lessons.title: Which fruit do you like?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will choose between two fruits and stand in the line for their choice.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort objects, count to five with support and say more and fewer.
resources: Pictures of an orange and a mango
lessons.starter: Show pictures of an orange and a mango. Say "Which do you like? Orange or mango? Stand by the picture you like."
teacherActivities: Put the two pictures at the end of two lines. Say "If you like oranges, stand here."
Ask the children in each line to stand neatly one behind another.
Say "Let us look at the lines. Which line is longer?"
Count the children in each line together.
learnerActivities: Children choose a picture and walk to it.
Children line up behind the picture.
Children look and point to the longer line.
Children count each line aloud.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the two pictures at the end of two lines. Say "If you like oranges, stand here." Children: Children choose a picture and walk to it.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask the children in each line to stand neatly one behind another. Children: Children line up behind the picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Let us look at the lines. Which line is longer?" Children: Children look and point to the longer line.
Step 4. Teacher: Count the children in each line together. Children: Children count each line aloud.

practical.title: Fruit lines
steps: Make two lines on the floor.
Each child chooses a fruit and stands in a line.
practical.safety: Keep lines short with space between children; walk calmly; no pushing.

differentiation.support: Choose with an adult and stand together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess which line will be longer before counting.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Count both lines and say "More oranges" or "More mangoes."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask family members which food they like and count how many choose each.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose between two fruits and stand in the line for their choice" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Blocks in lines
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will place blocks in two lines and say which line has more.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort objects, count to five with support and say more and fewer.
lessons.starter: Show a pile of red and blue blocks and say "Let us put the reds in one line and the blues in another line. Which will have more?"
teacherActivities: Sort the blocks by colour into two lines starting at the same end.
Look at the two lines. Say "This line has more."
Count both lines and say the numbers.
Let children choose two colours and make their own lines.
learnerActivities: Children sort the blocks into lines.
Children point to the longer line.
Children count and compare.
Pairs make lines and say which has more.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sort the blocks by colour into two lines starting at the same end. Children: Children sort the blocks into lines.
Step 2. Teacher: Look at the two lines. Say "This line has more." Children: Children point to the longer line.
Step 3. Teacher: Count both lines and say the numbers. Children: Children count and compare.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children choose two colours and make their own lines. Children: Pairs make lines and say which has more.

practical.title: Block graph
steps: Give each pair a pile of blocks in two colours.
practical.safety: Use large blocks only; keep them on the mat; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Sort two colours and compare lines with one block in each.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count each line and say how many more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Count both lines one more time and say "More red" or "More blue."
lessons.homeConnection: Sort spoons and cups into lines at home and compare.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "place blocks in two lines and say which line has more" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our shoes graph
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort shoes into two groups and count each line.
successCriteria: Counts a line of up to five
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort objects, count to five with support and say more and fewer.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us make a shoe graph. Who is wearing sandals? Who is wearing closed shoes?" Ask children to take off one shoe.
teacherActivities: Put the sandal picture and the closed shoe picture on the floor. Place your own shoe in a line.
Line up the shoes neatly one beside another. Say "Let us count each line."
Remove two shoes from one line and count again.
learnerActivities: Children place their shoes under the matching picture.
Children count the shoes in each line.
Children point to the line with more.
Children count again and say the new number.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the sandal picture and the closed shoe picture on the floor. Place your own shoe in a line. Children: Children place their shoes under the matching picture.
Step 2. Teacher: Line up the shoes neatly one beside another. Say "Let us count each line." Children: Children count the shoes in each line.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which line has more shoes?" Children: Children point to the line with more.
Step 4. Teacher: Remove two shoes from one line and count again. Children: Children count again and say the new number.

practical.title: Shoe lines
steps: Children place one shoe in the correct line.
practical.safety: Keep shoes in neat lines and away from walkways; children wash hands after handling shoes.

differentiation.support: Count only the shorter line with an adult.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess how many shoes are in each line and then count.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put shoes back and say "Sandals and shoes, all done."
lessons.homeConnection: Sort shoes by type at the door and count each group.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort shoes into two groups and count each line" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our favourite game graph
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will vote with a block for a favourite game and say which has more.
successCriteria: Places a block in the matching stack
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort objects, count to five with support and say more and fewer.
resources: Two pictures of games (ball and dance)
lessons.starter: Show pictures of ball play and dancing. Say "Which game do you like best? Put a block on your favourite."
teacherActivities: Give each child a block. Ask them to put it by their favourite picture.
Build a tall tower under each picture, one block at a time.
Ask "Which tower is taller?" and "Which has more blocks?"
Count the blocks in each tower.
learnerActivities: Children place a block under a picture.
Children watch the towers grow.
Children point to the taller tower.
Children count and say the numbers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give each child a block. Ask them to put it by their favourite picture. Children: Children place a block under a picture.
Step 2. Teacher: Build a tall tower under each picture, one block at a time. Children: Children watch the towers grow.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which tower is taller?" and "Which has more blocks?" Children: Children point to the taller tower.
Step 4. Teacher: Count the blocks in each tower. Children: Children count and say the numbers.

practical.title: Block vote
steps: Place it in a stack for their favourite game.
practical.safety: Use large blocks; build towers on the floor; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Choose with an adult and place the block together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say which game won and how they know.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Say "More blocks, more friends like it" and then play the winning game.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a family graph of favourite foods using spoons or sticks held by an adult.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "vote with a block for a favourite game and say which has more" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Graph stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can sort, compare and count lines at three stations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort objects, count to five with support and say more and fewer.
lessons.starter: Sing the sorting song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Which line has more?" and "How many are in this line?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child compares and counts.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which line has more?" and "How many are in this line?" Children: Child compares and counts.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use large items only; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to run a vote for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: joins a group according to a choice; says which line has more; counts a short line.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Sing the sorting song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a simple graph at home with family members.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can sort, compare and count lines at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
